newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS PCC CHIEF SEES FAST REVENUE GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS PCC CHIEF SEES FAST REVENUE GROWTH.

text.p: PCC, Philips Electronics NV's consumer communications products joint venture with Lucent Technologies, can grow its revenues by much more than market growth rates, its chief said on Monday.

"I would expect the future revenues of the business to grow much faster than the market growth. We're going to be in the top three (in the world market) by the year 2000," PCC chief executive Mike McTighe told journalists at a briefing.
Philips and Lucent said last week they were merging their consumer communications products businesses into the 60/40 PCC venture, which would have a $2.5 billion a year turnover.
"Last year the market we're talking about was in excess of $20 billion and it's growing at around 15 percent per annum in revenue terms," McTighe said.
The market was set to boom as sales of personal communications equipment rocketed, driven by the demand for mobile communications, particularly cellular phones, he said.

Mobile phone ownership at the end of last year was around 1.6 percent of the world's population, McTighe said. "We haven't seen the market yet. That's not the penetration you would expect of a normal consumer device," he added -- pointing to penetrations of around 28 percent of populations in Scandinavia.
Synergies between the partners in the venture were enormous, with very few overlaps between the Dutch consumer electronics giant and the huge U.S. telecoms equipment maker, he said.

"The deal was done in a record time because there was so much synergy, very little duplication, tremendous complementarity, geographically, technologically and in distribution. It just made a lot of sense, the more we talked the more sense it made," McTighe said.
"This is a great alliance, it's one plus one equals three."
He said Philips chairman Cor Boonstra had been closely involved in the Lucent talks which had kicked off "literally a few weeks ago".

"It's all part of the (Boonstra) strategy. He's always believed we needed a growth strategy -- restructuring is absolutely necessary and will continue to be necessary -- but you can't run a business just on restructuring, you have to grow," McTighe said.
Philips' profile would be raised enormously by the move to market consumer communications products in the U.S. under the Philips brand, he said.

"Philips has around $2.0 billion of consumer electronics businesses in North America and this adds another $1.1 billion...By definition it's got to give Philips a big jump up in terms of that whole brand structure," McTighe said.
"It's an indication of what the company means...that it's willing to do these things, to go after alliances and make these things work." -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
